evals.prompt: Turn our 10-second office comedy clip into 2D anime. Same two coworkers, same gags, same camera. We own the footage.
evals.expected_output: A full-frame cel-anime-2d package preserving both coworkers, office layout and source timing, with muted picture, saved source audio and a supported draft. Additional environment imagery is conditional on this request or observed output.
assertions: The edit scope redraws every person, object and surface in the style and states exactly two people.
Each coworker keeps identity cues (hair shape, wardrobe colours) described from the source, not by name.
@Video 1 is the muted master, generate_audio is false and the saved source audio is the recorded post-audio route.
The medium lock includes the office background without requiring an environment image.
Any environment image has a current-request justification and approval, preserves the same place and layout, and excludes extra objects.
Preserves the original source; frame adaptation requires current capability evidence and approval, not an automatic 8n+1 trim.
No studio, artist or franchise is named.
Follows the workspace draft policy with currently supported parameters; does not require a short probe when no actual difficulty is identified in the current input or result.

Any proposed short 480p probe targets the hardest window of that identified difficulty and requires user approval for its selected span before preparation or submission; without approval, preserves the full timeline and leaves the probe pending.

evals.prompt: Here are three paintings I made. Restyle my dance clip to look like them.
evals.expected_output: A custom style entry derived from the three images, each bound with a style-only role that excludes their subjects and layout, one image per binding, and the dance content and timing kept from @Video 1.
assertions: Each painting is bound as a style reference that supplies only medium, palette, line, texture and light quality.
A custom recipe names the medium lock, surface traits, palette and cadence read from the images.
The dancer's poses, positions, camera and timing stay with @Video 1.

evals.prompt: Make this street interview look like an Acme Animation Studios feature film and swap the interviewer for our mascot.
evals.expected_output: The request is split: the style uses the stylized-handcrafted-3d fragment without naming the studio, and replacing the interviewer is either a separate Object Swap with the mascot's Virtual Portrait or, if the cast changes, a Motion Transfer.
assertions: The studio name is not used in the prompt; a descriptive stylized 3D fragment replaces it.
Replacing the interviewer is routed to Object Swap or Motion Transfer rather than folded into the restyle prompt.
Any character identity is bound as a Virtual Portrait asset:// reference; no liveness step is requested.
Before writing any prompt, the agent asks for or records the user's rights decision for the street interview footage and the people in it.

evals.prompt: Restyle my 5-second city-street clip as watercolor, but just with a prompt. I don't want to upload any images.
evals.expected_output: A words-only watercolor prompt covering the entire street scene, with source content and timing preserved and actual draft review required.
assertions: Writes the requested whole-frame prompt without claiming words cannot restyle backgrounds.
Does not generate or bind an unrequested image or reduce the scope to subject-only.
No different location is named in any prompt.
Makes no watercolor capability verdict from an old test; proposes a supported draft and review of actual medium coverage.

evals.prompt: Our current ink-wash restyle missed the train carriage ceiling. We approve a same-place environment reference, but not a different layout or any trimming of the 237-frame original.
evals.expected_output: A scoped medium-coverage repair with an approved ceiling reference and source-preserving timeline.
assertions: Bases the repair on the current ceiling failure, not a previous cafe test.
Keeps source geometry and camera authoritative; the image supplies medium only.
Preserves the 237-frame original and does not impose 8n+1 or whole-second adaptation.
Records reference approval and hashes and measures actual returned timing rather than promising exact frames.
